meta.name: Catch soft 404 and error pages from sitemaps with Snapshot Site, Slack, and Google Sheets

name: Sitemap Soft 404 & Error Page Catcher → Slack

parameters.content:
## Find Soft 404s: Pages Serving an Error With HTTP 200

### How it works

Once a day this workflow fetches your site's own **`sitemap.xml`**, extracts every `<loc>` URL with a regex, caps and samples the list, then runs one Snapshot Site **Analyze** call per sampled URL with `enableQuality: true`. Each page is classified from the verified response fields: `hard-error` (`quality.httpStatus >= 400`), `blank` (`quality.isBlank`), `captcha` (`quality.hasCaptcha`), and the headline case — **`soft-error`**: a non-error HTTP status served together with error-page content, detected by matching `metadata.title` and `headings.h1` against the `ERROR_PAGE_PATTERNS` constant in **Detect Error Page**.

That soft case is the reason this template exists. A styled "Page not found" template returned with a **200** status is invisible to every status-code monitor and every uptime checker — they all report the page as healthy, because technically it is. Google calls the same thing a soft 404 and quietly drops the URL from the index.

The URL list comes from the sitemap rather than a hand-maintained watchlist on purpose: a soft-404 sweep that only covers pages you already thought to list is worthless, because the broken ones are the pages nobody remembers. `MAX_URLS` (50 by default) caps the cost, and the sample **rotates daily** so a 5,000-URL sitemap is covered completely over successive runs instead of the same first 50 URLs being audited forever. Every digest states how many URLs were audited out of how many were found, so coverage is never overstated.

One unreachable URL is recorded as `unreachable` and the sweep continues. A failed **sitemap** fetch is the opposite: it throws to a Slack alert, because a sweep that audited nothing must never look like a clean sweep.

### Setup steps

- Install the `n8n-nodes-snapshot-site` community node (Settings → Community nodes → Install → `n8n-nodes-snapshot-site`) — verified by n8n.
- Add a Snapshot Site credential, a Slack credential, and a Google Sheets credential.
- Open **Fetch Sitemap** and replace the `url` with your own sitemap, e.g. `https://example.com/sitemap.xml`. Include the scheme — the Snapshot Site API rejects bare domains with `Url must match format "uri"`.
- If that URL is a **sitemap index** (its `<loc>` entries end in `.xml`), the run stops with an explicit alert: only the first level is read. Point it at one child sitemap, or duplicate the fetch per child.
- Open **Extract Sitemap URLs** and set `MAX_URLS` (cost cap) plus `SAMPLE_MODE` (`rotate` / `spread` / `first`).
- Create a **Soft 404 Findings** tab, type its header row in literally — `url`, `status`, `signal`, `httpStatus`, `title`, `h1`, `isBlank`, `hasCaptcha`, `screenshotLink`, `checkedAt`, `sitemapUrl`, `totalFound`, `auditedCount`, `coverageNote` — then set the node's Mapping Column Mode to **"Map Automatically"** after import. Sheets column mappings never survive a JSON import.
- Set the channel on all three Slack nodes.

### Customization

The heuristic lives in exactly two constants in **Detect Error Page**: `ERROR_PAGE_PATTERNS` (add your template's own wording and languages) and `KNOWN_GOOD_URLS` (exempt a real page legitimately titled "404 errors explained"). `EXCLUDE_PATTERNS` in **Extract Sitemap URLs** drops whole URL families before they cost an Analyze call. `enableSummary` is deliberately `false`: an AI summary costs money and answers nothing here, since an error page is detected from status, title, headings and blankness.

## Fetch the sitemap and pick the URLs to audit

The sitemap URL is a plain string on **Fetch Sitemap** — edit it there. The response is read as **text**, and a regex pulls the `<loc>` values out; no XML node needed.
**Extract Sitemap URLs** dedupes, drops non-http entries, detects a sitemap index (only the first level is read), then caps at `MAX_URLS` and **rotates** the sample daily so the whole site is eventually covered.
A sitemap that cannot be fetched or parsed throws to the Slack alert below — a run that audited nothing must never be mistaken for a clean sweep.

## Analyze each URL and handle errors

One Analyze call per URL with `enableQuality: true` and `enableSummary: false` (the AI summary costs money and answers nothing here).
**Detect Error Page** reads the verified fields — `quality.httpStatus`, `quality.isBlank`, `quality.hasCaptcha`, `metadata.title`, `headings.h1` — and classifies each URL as `ok` / `hard-error` / `soft-error` / `blank` / `captcha`, recording **which signal fired**.
Hard failures (error output) and soft failures (`{error: true}` on the success output) both become an `unreachable` row and return to the loop, so one bad URL never aborts the sweep.

## Report the error pages

On the loop's Done branch every finding is appended to Google Sheets (queryable over time) and rendered as **one** Slack digest listing only the problem URLs with the signal that fired.
The digest always states how many URLs were audited out of how many were found — partial coverage reported as a clean site is the one failure mode a sweep like this must not have.
A clean run posts a short all-clear rather than staying silent: because coverage is partial and daily, "nothing happened" is genuinely informative here.
